title: Waaree’s Q2 Revenue Up 24%, Aims to Expand US Module Plant Capacity to 4.8 GW
summary: Solar module manufacturer Waaree Energies reported revenue from operations of ₹75.18 billion (~$783.13 million) in the second quarter (Q2) of the financial year (FY) 2027, a 23.9% year-over-year (YoY) increase from ₹60.66 billion (~$631.88 million).

direction_reasons: CAPACITY_EXPANSION cuts both ways — growth against capital, cost or execution risk
watch_next: demand visibility for the new capacity
WAAREEENER.why_it_matters: This is news about the company itself. The parts of the business most likely touched are capacity, balance sheet. Classified as capacity expansion.

ai_analysis.revenue_effect: Q2 revenue growth of 24% demonstrates strong immediate top-line traction. In the long term, expanding US module capacity to 4.8 GW provides a path to capture higher-value US dollar revenues and meet sustained demand from US utility-scale and commercial solar developers.
ai_analysis.margin_effect: Unclear in the short term, as US expansion requires upfront operating expenses and ramp-up costs. In the medium to long term, US manufacturing can command premium pricing and benefit from US tax incentives (such as IRA Section 45X credits), which could expand gross and EBITDA margins once full operational scale is reached.
ai_analysis.cost_effect: Capital expenditure will increase to fund the US manufacturing footprint expansion. Operational expenditure will also rise due to higher labor, facility, and regulatory compliance costs associated with operating in the US market compared to India.
ai_analysis.competitive_effect: Expanding US-based module manufacturing capacity to 4.8 GW enhances Waaree's competitive positioning against both pure-exporter Indian peers and international suppliers seeking compliant access to the US market amid ongoing trade restrictions on direct Chinese imports.
ai_analysis.regulatory_effect: Directly exposes the company to US trade policies, including tariffs, Foreign Entity of Concern (FEOC) rules, and requirements under the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) for domestic content and manufacturing tax credits.
ai_analysis.short_term: Positive earnings momentum from Q2 revenue growth (24% year-over-year). Management focus will center on finalizing capital allocation, site logistics, and permitting for the expanded US capacity over the next 0-3 months.
ai_analysis.medium_long_term: Successful execution of the 4.8 GW US capacity expansion will scale total global delivery capacity, diversify geographical revenue mix, and establish Waaree as a major onshore US module supplier over a multi-year horizon.
ai_analysis.second_order_effects: Higher reliance on compliant cell supply chains to feed the US assembly lines, potentially requiring further vertical integration or long-term supply agreements for non-targeted solar cells and components.
ai_analysis.key_uncertainty: The total CapEx required, commissioning timeline, and long-term regulatory stability of US IRA tax incentives and import tariffs.
monitor_next: Detailed timeline and CapEx budget for the 4.8 GW US module plant expansion.
Updates on solar cell sourcing strategy to feed the US manufacturing facility.
Quarterly module shipment volume and average selling prices (ASPs) in the US market.
Regulatory developments regarding US IRA Section 45X tax credits and trade tariffs on solar components.
